conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: Both outputs complete the install → authenticate → preview path with correct commands and all required states evidenced. A wins on fact fidelity and retrieval structure: every capability statement in A is traceable to the supplied facts, its page section order matches the sidebar order (Get started, Guides, CLI reference, Configuration, CI, Troubleshooting), its stub sections redirect the reader to Get started and the CLI reference instead of dead-ending, and its quickstart makes the plan/apply distinction explicit in text ('it is the only command in this workflow that publishes anything') plus Does-not-publish/Publishes badges repeated in the reference table. B has the stronger visual treatment — side-by-side preview-vs-publish comparison cards, copy buttons on every command, a cleaner heading outline — but it asserts 'Preview only — nothing leaves your machine' in the safety-critical comparison card, a capability the facts do not supply (they only support 'previews without publishing'), its body section order diverges from its own nav order, and its Guides/CI sections are dead-end placeholders ('Task-based guides live here'). Given the scenario's stated consequence (a misleading quickstart causes failed releases or abandonment) and the instruction not to award a win for decorative treatment, A's tighter adherence to the closed fact set outweighs B's superior visual hierarchy.
suspected_unblinding: B's app.js contains comments referencing coded requirement IDs (e.g. 'C2/A3/A4 — Search (client-side index over this page's own content; required state: no-results)'), which suggests one build followed a coded checklist or method. I do not know which treatment such codes map to and did not use this in judging; recorded per instructions.

The supplied facts only establish that plan does not publish; asserting fully local behavior overstates safety in exactly the place the scenario says a misleading claim causes harm (a developer on a restricted network or with confidentiality constraints could act on it). Fix: restate as 'previews without publishing', matching the facts.
